key_insight: A conditional diffusion framework that jointly models multiple cardiovascular biomarkers, enabling realistic cross-modal synthesis and imputation while preserving physiological relationships across signals.
problem_solved: Integrates heterogeneous cardiovascular monitoring modalities (different sampling rates, noise profiles, and missing channels) by learning their joint distribution so models can generate or impute missing modalities without large matched multimodal datasets.
method: Multivariate conditional diffusion model that learns the joint distribution of multiple cardiovascular biomarkers rather than separate unimodal generators.
Cross-modal conditioning and a shared latent representation to enable synthesis, imputation, and modality translation across signals with variable timing and missing channels.
Physiological-consistency constraints and task-aware training (e.g., downstream prediction or cycle-consistency) to keep synthesized signals clinically plausible and useful.
impact: Provides a practical route for robust data augmentation, cross-modal imputation, and simulation in cardiovascular ML, lowering data-collection burdens and improving model generalization and downstream clinical utility.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multimodal inputs (ECG/PPG/BP/others) → conditional diffusion module → joint synthesized outputs/imputations
Before/after example panels showing missing-channel imputation and cross-modal translation (real vs. synthesized signals)
Metric bar chart comparing fidelity and physiological correlation for real vs. synthesized biomarkers across evaluation datasets
Latent-space visualization (e.g., t-SNE) showing clustering by physiological state and modality, illustrating shared representation
